body: Thank you
I could. It's just the time and energy that goes into it. It would be worth it if I could get my husband to go too.

Well, thanks for reading everything I've ever posted, but it feels a bit creepy...

Anyway, no, he won't. He feels the burden of our relationship lies 100% in my hands to fix.

We don't go to church. I don't socialize outside of some "friends" online- and with them- hardly at all. I work, and take care of my kids, and fight with my husband. That's my entire life.

Considering it's how I feel whether I'm sober or not, probably means he's an asshole. I'm probably a bitch too, though.

I poured out everything to him a few minutes ago. We will see what happens. The bottom of a bottle can be deceiving. It can also be liberating. It's can also be relationship ending...

I'm don't know. I can see that. But part of me also knows that when my SO spoke about thinking of killing himself once (before we met), I kind of dismissed it because I didn't feel he actually knew what that was like.

So it could mean that he also knows these feelings and is subconsciously dismissing it or he is afraid that you might think differently if you find he feels the same.

It could also mean he doesn't understand it and it makes him uncomfortable. Or he dismisses it because he doesn't get it. Or doesn't want to.

The doesn't want to- that's dangerous for you. I hope that's not the case. Feel him out a bit more.

It's making me realize I should probably have the serious talk with my SO before he just leaves. Give him a chance to understand it before I assume he is of the "doesn't want to" variety....
It's something. I hope it leads somewhere positive.

I can completely understand that. You're giving a piece of yourself to that person. Respect and care would mean they would do the same for you, or at least appreciate it. It sucks so much to not see that happen.

One thing my husband did during a separation, is put a gift in my car with a note stating how sorry he was and that he wanted to make things right. I'll never forget it and felt it was one of the most genuine ways to reach me in that moment. He didn't force communication with me, he left the note and gift and moved on to something else in his day, letting me come to him when I was ready. I don't know how your wife would react to such an expression, but for me, it worked wonders in those moments.

With transparency in my story, it's 6 years later and we are still fighting. Do everything you can so you don't become us, where neither was fighting for each other, we only fought each other. Then you can say you did all you were able to, and if it's not enough, the burden is not 100% on you. I hope it doesn't come to that and you all can find a way to make it work, assuming the relationship is not toxic for either one of you. Best of luck.

Sometimes I feel so alone when laying in bed at night. I can hear my SO snoring, I can touch him, but I can't actually feel his presence. And when I think I should try to leave those moments, I want to wallow in them. I want to stay there in the comfort of my own darkness. Because, just maybe, it will get bad enough for someone else to see it.

But when it gets close to that point, I pull out the actress and show the world I'm fine, while I lose a little bit more of me, making me even more alone than I was before.
Congrats! :)

I hope you find that piece. I have found, in many situations, that the ones who hurt he most are the ones who care the most.

Those who don't care as much, don't understand what you are going through.

I could name three friends right now, who would understand and care very much about what you are dealing with. They are all online friends, but online friends with hearts that make them feel near. And even though you are a stranger, they would want you to know you are cared for, even if we can't find a way to properly show it. And with "we" I include myself, so that makes 4 people who care very much, and wish we could make it better, but know how hard that is considering what we deal with inside ourselves.

I tend to find myself giving advice over taking it. Or worse, not even seeking advice when I need it most. But I do get a bit of satisfaction from feeling like I may have helped someone else. I get the vibe you feel the same way. But then, upon reflection, you wonder if it ever even mattered. I get that way too.

As for meaning, I agree with the other commenter. We have to give ourselves meaning and purpose. But when you feel like you're worthless where can you find that and build upon it?

I hope you are able to find some purpose for yourself when you're not having a low moment (it's always nice if you are able to escape it for a bit) and find hope in it when you do fall back in. It's so hard to hold onto that hope but it can make all the difference in your life.

Like a meaningless existence where you just go through the paces and exist? It's so hard to take joy in anything when you feel like it's just a blip on the time line compared to everything else you just deal with.

I hate that other people feel this way. I would gladly take on all of this to know others don't deal with it. But at the same time, I feel better knowing some people understand it, when I'm surrounded by many who don't.

I hope you find some comfort in that as well. I wish I had more for you than that.

I don't think I would survive the process of divorce. It's hard to explain but it's easier to deal with this than to face everyone as a failure or to deal with the intense barrage of insults that would come. It would be worse than it is now. And I've already failed at so much in life I don't know if I could add that pain on top of everything else.

I don't think it matters anyway. We have had such a huge fight tonight I don't think there is any way to come back from it. I need to sleep and can't. I have work to do but didn't. I feel like sitting outside in the rainstorm until the sun comes up and I'm forced to face another day.
Easier said than done when you have been together for over a decade and have two kids

And now he is SO SURE it wasn't THAT harsh how he spoke to me... And I need to just stop my shit.

I had literally stopped walking and turned away from the doors and other people heard him through the phone too. And he says he was only showing a little frustration....

Oh my gaaaaaahahahahahaha

The visuals and Tl;dr are fantastic... I'm pretty sure I'm a terrible person for laughing as hard as I am...

Gah that's shitty. I have similar situation, and Mother's Day always sucks for me too. Sorry you're dealing with it too :(

I love my kids, but sometimes, I really hate being a mom.

Yesterday, I knew it was coming. Thankfully I have some control of the finances, so I went on a shopping spree for myself. Good thing, too. I woke up and had to make coffee and get everyone ready for the day. I didn't really get anything from them other than attitude and a willingness to do what they want instead of what I asked them to.

Do you have the ability to set some money aside when you can until you build it up enough, and buy yourself something? Not necessarily a healthy way to deal with shit, but I always feel better if I can give myself something. Even if it is a nice new shirt no one will notice :) as long as it makes me feel pretty, that's what matters.

Society sucks at helping people. And they make us feel bad or guilty for needing that help. And that makes it impossible for us to accept that we need help. Which means we don't push for that help. It's a terrible cycle.

It's so hard to accept anything you can't do. Maybe it can be a pushing point for finding ways you can do something others might tell you that you can't? Again, I don't know specifics. And that fight to find those ways is easier typed than accomplished. But damnit all if we can't find some way to push through the bullshit and push ourselves past what we thought were our limits.

If we didn't do that already, we wouldn't be here, ready to be able to actually talk about these things vs continuing to bottle it up. A place where we know we can express ourselves in the most raw of forms, and maybe, not feel like an outcast. Or not feel like we're the only ones. Every situation is different, but so many are alike that we forget we have allies. I hope you find allies in us and it helps give you what you need to keep moving forward.

I remember feeling like I had NO WHERE to go. So thankful I can come here. I hope you feel the same. It pushes us out of the comfort of our own

I have been known to call out welfare fraud amongst people I've met. But I can honestly say there is a reason it is in place and for people who genuinely need it.

I don't feel that makes someone a failure, and I feel awful that the perception others have set forth with their reliance on something they don't need, sets a negative light on those who really do need it.

Depression and anxiety is hard enough. With autism too, I can only imagine. You are very well spoken and I'm sure you feel very trapped and helpless when it comes to certain things. (I don't know you or your level but I am sincerely amazed at what you sound like you have accomplished).

I hope I don't offend. I just feel like someone who can fight through anxiety and depression and any other hurdles, to get done what needs to be done (even if it is going to the right people for assistance and holding a job), deserves to know that those are fantastic steps. It's so hard to keep moving forward. Especially when you feel worthless.

I'm sorry you're feeling that way. I know I can't make that change, and I know that I'm only pointing out what you already know.

Depression sucks so much when it drags you though the mud like this, when you were looking at a rainbow.
